leverage_rationale: Structured test/run/failure/recovery state materially improves agent reliability and prevents guessing when browser selectors fail.

impact_rationale: Browser-test brittleness is a concrete problem for developers and QA teams, and evidence-backed recovery plus reusable tests directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets brittle browser failures and reusable Playwright regression tests.
Visible workflow connects failure evidence to recovery and verification.
creativity_rationale: The verified-recovery-to-regression-test loop is a fresh, safety-conscious synthesis of browser automation and WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Avoids blind selector guessing and requires evidence of a safe fallback.
Combines recovery with durable test export.
usability_note: The staged control-plane flow appears understandable and status-driven; some small text is hard to read.
red_flags: Agent invocation itself is not clearly visible in the supplied frames.
Some detailed output text is too small to independently read.
standouts: Evidence-preserving recovery rather than agent guessing.

advance_reason: Strong demonstrated product workflow and unusually direct WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A system that learns agent tools from human demonstrations and gates irreversible actions with WebAuthn.
what_it_does: Deputy synthesizes typed WebMCP tools from demonstrations, blocks risky calls until a physical passkey approval, quarantines untrusted content, and writes an audit log.
leverage_rationale: The product changes what WebMCP can safely mean: humans author capabilities through demonstrations, and an agent cannot forge consent because approval is cryptographically bound to exact tool arguments.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows human demonstration, tool synthesis, agent risky call refusal, and passkey gate.
About text specifies WebAuthn challenge binding to tool/version/arguments and single-use commit.
Quarantine and hash-chained audit log address agent security boundaries.
execution_rationale: A 190-second video with a narrated demonstration provides strong claimed workflow evidence across synthesis, refusal, approval, and audit concepts, though narration notes some functionality as being added and exact live behavior is not independently observed.
execution_evidence: video=True, 190 seconds, with transcript covering human demonstration and risky refund flow.
Public repository and live demo reported.
Description names concrete TypeScript/Hono/React/WebAuthn architecture.
impact_rationale: Agent safety, consent authenticity, and capability authoring are high-value problems for developers and organizations deploying tool-using agents.
impact_evidence: Targets forged human approval and dangerous irreversible actions.
Provides passkey-bound consent, provenance quarantine, and tamper-evident auditability.
creativity_rationale: Learning typed tools from ordinary human demonstrations combined with physically unforgeable consent and quarantine is an exceptionally ambitious, memorable interaction and security model.
creativity_evidence: Semantic demonstration-to-tool synthesis avoids hand coding.
Exact-argument WebAuthn binding and single-use commit are distinctive safeguards.

usability_note: Demonstration-based authoring promises low-code capability creation; passkey flows may add friction but appropriately so for risk.
red_flags: Transcript says some agent-prevention functionality is still being added.
Security claims are not independently audited here.
standouts: Human-authored tools without code.

advance_reason: Outstanding leverage, safety relevance, and originality with substantial video evidence.
